```{r set up}
#| echo: false
#| error: false
pacman::p_load(dplyr, janitor,ggplot2, fingertipsR, leaflet, sf,
               gt, gtExtras, plotly, purrr, readr, patchwork, flextable, reactable, grid, htmlwidgets)
#flextable, kable
source("C:/nhs-nwl-icb-health-equity/src/data_cleaning.R")
source("C:/nhs-nwl-icb-health-equity/src/plot_theme.R")
source("C:/nhs-nwl-icb-health-equity/src/geography_functions.R")

#output_path <- "C:/nwlicb/outputs/health_equity_outcomes/"
old_date <- "2019"
new_date <-"2025"

## General data 
nwl_code_list <- get_north_west_london_code()
msoa_shape <- ingest_shape_date(geography="msoa", filter_codes = nwl_code_list$msoa_codes_11, all_codes = nwl_code_list$nwl_all_codes  %>% distinct(msoa11cd, msoa21cd))
lad_shape <- ingest_shape_date(geography="lad", filter_codes = nwl_code_list$lad_codes_21, all_codes = nwl_code_list$nwl_all_codes)
lsoa_shape <- ingest_shape_date(geography="lsoa", filter_codes = nwl_code_list$lsoa_codes_21, all_codes = nwl_code_list$nwl_all_codes)

boroughs <-c("Westminster", "Ealing", "Brent", "Kensington and Chelsea", "Hammersmith and Fulham", "Harrow", "Hounslow","Hillingdon")

#colors
nhs_blue <- "#005EB8"

               ,"#1E7F66"
               ,"#905E26"
               ,"#7A9AC9")
```

```{r data processing}

# Data --------------------------------------------------------------------


imd_old <- readxl::read_excel("data/imd/File_2_-_IoD2019_Domains_of_Deprivation.xlsx", sheet = 2) %>% 
  janitor::clean_names()

imd_new <- readxl::read_excel("data/imd/File_2_IoD2025_Domains_of_Deprivation.xlsx", sheet = 2) %>% 
  janitor::clean_names()

nwl_lsoa_population_2021 <- read.csv("data/imd/population_data.csv")
nwl_lsoa_population_2011 <-  nwl_lsoa_population_2021%>% 
  dplyr::left_join(nwl_code_list$nwl_all_codes %>% 
                     distinct(lsoa11cd, lsoa21cd, lad22cd, lad22nm, msoa21cd, msoa11cd),
                   by=c("geography_code" ="lsoa21cd")) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(lsoa11cd) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(obs_value=sum(obs_value))




# Data process ------------------------------------------------------------


imd_nwl_old <- imd_old %>% 
  dplyr::inner_join(nwl_code_list$nwl_all_codes %>% 
                      distinct(lsoa11cd, lsoa21cd),
                    by=c("lsoa_code_2011"="lsoa11cd"))

imd_nwl_new <- imd_new %>% 
  dplyr::inner_join(nwl_code_list$nwl_all_codes %>% 
                      distinct(lsoa21cd),
                    by=c("lsoa_code_2021"="lsoa21cd")) 

imd_long <- imd_nwl_old %>% 
  dplyr::select(-contains("rank")) %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = contains("decile"),names_to = "domain", values_to = "decile") %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(nwl_lsoa_population_2011 %>% 
                     select(lsoa11cd, obs_value),
                   by=c("lsoa_code_2011"="lsoa11cd")) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(year=old_date) %>% 
  dplyr::bind_rows(imd_nwl_new %>% 
    dplyr::select(-contains("rank")) %>% 
    tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = contains("decile"), names_to = "domain", values_to = "decile") %>% 
    dplyr::left_join(nwl_lsoa_population_2021 %>% 
                       select(geography_code , obs_value),
                     by=c("lsoa_code_2021"="geography_code")) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(year=new_date)
    ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(is_core20=case_when(
    decile <= 2 ~ "Core 20",
    decile > 2 ~ "Other 80",
    TRUE ~ NA
  )) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(domain=sub("_decile.*", "", domain),
                domain=gsub("_", " ", domain))


imd_nwl_long <- imd_long %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(year, domain, is_core20) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(population=sum(obs_value)) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(year, domain) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(percentage=population/sum(population)*100) 
  

imd_nwl_differences <- imd_nwl_long %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(is_core20, domain), names_from = year, values_from = percentage) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(difference=`2025`-`2019`) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(is_core20=="Core 20") %>% 
  janitor::clean_names()

lsoa_imd_nwl <- lsoa_shape %>% 
  dplyr::full_join(imd_nwl_new, by=c("lsoa21cd"="lsoa_code_2021"))  %>% 
  sf::st_transform(crs = 4326) %>%
  dplyr::select(c(lsoa21cd, global_id, geometry, lad22cd, lad22nm, contains("decile")))

names(lsoa_imd_nwl) <- gsub("(_decile).*", "", names(lsoa_imd_nwl))

lad_shape <- lad_shape %>% 
  sf::st_transform(crs = 4326)

imd_wide <- imd_nwl_new  %>% 
  dplyr::select(lsoa_code_2021,local_authority_district_name_2024,index_of_multiple_deprivation_imd_decile_where_1_is_most_deprived_10_percent_of_lso_as) %>% 
  dplyr::rename("imd_2025"=index_of_multiple_deprivation_imd_decile_where_1_is_most_deprived_10_percent_of_lso_as) %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(imd_nwl_old %>% 
                     dplyr::select(lsoa_code_2011,, lsoa21cd,index_of_multiple_deprivation_imd_decile_where_1_is_most_deprived_10_percent_of_lso_as) %>% 
                     dplyr::rename("imd_2019"=index_of_multiple_deprivation_imd_decile_where_1_is_most_deprived_10_percent_of_lso_as),
                   by = c("lsoa_code_2021" ="lsoa21cd")) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(decile_diff=imd_2025-imd_2019) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(new_core20=ifelse((imd_2025 %in% c(1,2) & !imd_2019 %in% c(1,2)),1,0))

imd_diff_shape <- lsoa_shape %>% 
  dplyr::full_join(imd_wide, by=c("lsoa21cd"="lsoa_code_2021"), relationship="many-to-many")  %>% 
  sf::st_transform(crs = 4326) 


```
<div style="background-color:#005EB8; color:white; padding:1.5em; border-radius:10px;">

## Key Messages

* The percentage of the NWL population living in a Core 20 area has increased from 12.7% to 17.4%.
* Barriers to housing and services is the domain where the highest proportion of people live in a Core 20 area (57.5%); however, this is also an area that has shown improvement (fewer Core 20 areas in NWL).
* Only two domains have shown improvement (fewer people living in a Core 20 area) — crime and barriers to housing and services.
* The largest increase in people living in a Core 20 area is in the income domain.
* Of the eight boroughs, K&C, H&F, and Harrow have seen decreases in the proportion of their populations living in a Core 20 area.
* Brent has seen the largest increase in people living in a Core 20 area and now has the highest proportion of its population in the Core 20 across all boroughs (29.6%).
* Brent also reports the domain with the greatest worsening, with 28.9% more people now living in an income Core 20 area.
* K&C reports the greatest improvement in the barriers to housing domain, with a 55.9% decrease in people living in a Core 20 area for that domain.

### Key Health Messages
One of the domains of deprivation is Health and Disability - this makes up 13.5% of the overall deprivation indices.

* The health and disability domain is where NWL has the smallest proportion of its population living in a Core 20 area — only 2.8%. However, this has increased by 1.4% since 2019.
* Westminster has the greatest proportion of its population in a Core 20 area (12.5%) and  has seen the largest increase in people living in a Core 20 area (11.1%) since 2018.

</div>

<br>


## Introduction

The English Indices of Deprivation (IoD) 2025 provide a set of relative measures
of deprivation for small areas (Lower-layer Super Output Areas) across England,
based on seven different domains of deprivation. These domains are listed below along with the weight in which they make up the over deprivation score and example measures that are used to calculate rank and decile.

::: {.small-table}

| Domain                           	| Weight of domain 	| Example measures                          	|
|----------------------------------	|------------------	|------------------------------------------------------	|
| Income                           	| 22.5%            	| Adults and children in Income Support benefit units  	|
| Employment                       	| 22.5%            	| Claimants of Income Support                          	|
| Education, Skills and Training   	| 13.5%            	| Key Stage 2 attainment: scaled scores                	|
| Health and Disability            	| 13.5%            	| Years of Potential Life Lost                         	|
| Crime                            	| 9.3%             	| Violence with injury                                 	|
| Living Environment               	| 9.3%             	| Housing Energy Performance Score, Air Quality         	|
| Barriers to Housing and Services 	| 9.3%             	| Housing affordability                                	|

:::

See [‘The English Indices of Deprivation 2025: Technical Report’](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/english-indices-of-deprivation-2025-technical-report) for more details
about the creation of the indices and [‘The English Indices of Deprivation 2025:
Research Report'](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/english-indices-of-deprivation-2025-research-report) for national level analysis of the overall findings


## Core 20 summary

This report outlines the percentage of the North West London Population that lives in a Core 20 area across the overall deprivation score and the seven domains.

```{r text_boxes, results='asis'}

domains <- c("index of multiple deprivation imd", "income" ,                          
              "employment" ,                       "education skills and training",    
              "health deprivation and disability", "crime",                            
              "barriers to housing and services",  "living environment")  


imd_nwl_differences <- imd_nwl_differences %>% 
dplyr::mutate(domain=factor(domain, levels=domains)) %>% 
dplyr::arrange(domain)

cat('<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 20px;">\n')

# Loop through boxes
for(i in 1:nrow(imd_nwl_differences)){
  box_class <- ifelse(i == 1, "text-box text-box-first", "text-box")
  
  cat('<div class="', box_class, '">', sep = "")
  cat('<span class="number">', paste0(round(imd_nwl_differences$x2025[i],1),"%"), '</span><br>', sep = "")
  cat('<span class="description">',paste0("of our population live a ", imd_nwl_differences$domain[i], " Core 20 area."), '</span>', sep = "")
cat('<span class="description">',paste0("This is an ", round(imd_nwl_differences$difference[i],1), "% point change since 2019" ), '</span>', sep = "")
  cat('</div>\n')
}

# Close container div
cat('</div>')

```

## Deprivation map

The below map shows each lower super output area (LSOA) in NWL (~9,000) and the  deprivation decile assigned to each LSOA for the IMD score and each domain scores. Use the radio buttons to select a different domain. 

```{r maps, results='asis', cache=TRUE, fig.height=6}
#| echo: false
map <- leaflet(options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>% addTiles()
 
domains <- c("index_of_multiple_deprivation_imd", "income" ,                           
             "employment" ,                       "education_skills_and_training",     
             "health_deprivation_and_disability", "crime",                             
             "barriers_to_housing_and_services",  "living_environment")    

group_names <- gsub("_", " ", domains)

lsoa_simple <- rmapshaper::ms_simplify(lsoa_imd_nwl, keep = 0.05)
 
for (i in seq_along(domains)) { 
  
  col <- domains[i]
  grp <- group_names[i]
   
  pal <- colorNumeric( 
    palette = c("#A50026", "#D73027", "#F46D43", "#FDAE61", 
                "#FEE090", "#E0F3F8", "#ABD9E9", "#74ADD1", 
                "#4575B4", "#313695"), 
    domain = lsoa_simple[[col]], 
    na.color = "lightgrey"   # polygons with NA values will appear grey 
  ) 
  
    labels_vec <- paste0(grp, ": ",
                       ifelse(is.na(lsoa_simple[[col]]),
                              "NA",
                              round(lsoa_simple[[col]], 2)),
                       " Area: ", lsoa_simple$lsoa21cd)
   
  map <- map %>% 
    addPolygons( 
      data=lsoa_simple, 
      fillColor = pal(lsoa_simple[[col]]), 
      color = "black", 
      weight = 1, 
      fillOpacity = 0.7, 
      group = grp, 
      label = labels_vec,
      labelOptions = labelOptions(direction = "auto", textsize = "12px")
    ) 
  
   assign(paste0("pal_", col), pal, envir = .GlobalEnv)
   
} 

# Add layer control so user can toggle the 8 groups
map <- map %>%
   addPolygons(
    data = lad_shape,
    color = "black",
    weight = 3,
    fill = FALSE,
    opacity = 1,
    group = "Local Authority Boundaries"
  ) %>%
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups = group_names,  
    overlayGroups = c("Local Authority Boundaries"),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE) #radio buttons (mutually exclusive)
  )

# Choose initial visible group (e.g., first)
initial_visible <- group_names[1]
groups_to_hide <- setdiff(group_names, initial_visible)

# Hide all groups except the initial_visible one so the radio state matches visible layers
map <- map %>% hideGroup(groups_to_hide)

# Optionally add a legend for the initially visible group
first_col <- domains[1]
first_pal <- get(paste0("pal_", first_col))
map <- map %>%
  addLegend(
    pal = first_pal,
    #values=lsoa_simple$lsoa21cd,
    values = lsoa_simple[[first_col]],
    title = "Deprivation decile",
    position = "bottomright"
  )

# print the map (render once)
map
```
<br>


The below map shows the LSOA's which have changed deprivation decile since 2019. A increase in decile suggests movedment towards being a more affluent area, whereas a decrease means the area has become more deprived. The areas highlighted in orange represent te area who weren't a Core 20 area before but are now.


```{r diff_maps, results='asis', cache=TRUE, fig.height=6}

max_abs <- max(abs(range(imd_diff_shape$decile_diff, na.rm = TRUE)))
symmetric_domain <- c(-max_abs, max_abs)

custom_breaks <- c(-Inf, -3, -1, 0, 1, 3, Inf)
custom_labels <- c("Large decrease (<= -3)",
                   "Moderate decrease (-2)",
                   "Small decrease (-1)",
                   "No change (0)",
                   "Small increase (1)",
                   "Moderate increase (3)",
                   "Large increase (>= 3)")


palette_custom <- colorRampPalette(c("deeppink4", "white", "darkgreen"))(7)

pal_custom <- colorBin(palette = palette_custom,
                       domain = imd_diff_shape$decile_diff,
                       bins = custom_breaks,
                       na.color = "lightgrey",
                       right = FALSE)


map2<- leaflet(options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addPolygons(
    data = imd_diff_shape,
    fillColor = ~pal_custom(decile_diff),
    color = "black",
    weight = 1,
    fillOpacity = 0.8
  ) %>%
  addPolygons(
    data = lad_shape,
    color = "black",
    weight = 3,
    fill = FALSE
  ) %>%
    addPolygons(
    data =imd_diff_shape %>% dplyr::filter( new_core20==1),
    fillOpacity = 0.25,
    color = "orange",
    weight = 2,
    opacity = 1,
    group = "New Core 20 Areas",
    #label = ~paste0(ifelse(!is.null(name) , name, ifelse(!is.null(lsoa21nm), lsoa21nm, "")),
    #               " — New Core 20"),   # change name / label column as appropriate
    #labelOptions = labelOptions(direction = "auto", textsize = "12px")
  ) %>% 
  # use explicit colors+labels for the legend so wording matches bins
  addLegend(
    colors = palette_custom,
    labels = custom_labels,
    title = "Decile difference",
    position = "bottomright",
    opacity = 1
  ) %>% 
  addLegend(
    colors = "orange",
    labels = "New Core 20 LSOA",
    title = NULL,
    position = "bottomleft",
    opacity = 1,
    layerId = "legend_new_core20"
  ) %>%
  addLayersControl(
    #baseGroups = "IMD",                       # your choropleth groups
    overlayGroups = c("New Core 20 Areas"),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  )

map2

```

## Borough Core 20 summary 

The below details for each borough the percentage of people living in the Core 20 for each domain. When a domain isn't listed it means there are no Core 20 areas for that domain in the borough.

::: panel-tabset

```{r borough_text_boxes, results='asis'}

boroughs <- c("Brent" , "Ealing", "Hammersmith and Fulham","Harrow" , "Hillingdon" ,"Hounslow","Kensington and Chelsea" ,"Westminster")

domains <- c("index of multiple deprivation imd", "income" ,                          
              "employment" ,                       "education skills and training",    
              "health deprivation and disability", "crime",                            
              "barriers to housing and services",  "living environment")  

for (bh in boroughs) { 

  cat("###", gsub("_", " ", bh), "\n\n")

  imd_bh_long <- imd_long %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(lad=ifelse(year==2025, local_authority_district_name_2024, local_authority_district_name_2019)) %>% 
    dplyr::filter(lad==bh) %>% 
    dplyr::group_by(year, domain, is_core20) %>% 
    dplyr::summarise(population=sum(obs_value),
                     n_lsoas=n()) %>% 
    dplyr::group_by(year, domain) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(percentage=population/sum(population)*100,
                  lsoa_percentage=n_lsoas/sum(n_lsoas)*100) 
  
  imd_bh_differences <- imd_bh_long %>% 
    tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(is_core20, domain), names_from = year, values_from = percentage) %>% 
    janitor::clean_names() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(x2019=ifelse(is.na(x2019), 0,x2019),
                  x2025=ifelse(is.na(x2025), 0,x2025)) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(difference=x2025-x2019) %>% 
    dplyr::filter(is_core20=="Core 20") %>% 
    janitor::clean_names()
   
  imd_bh_differences <- imd_bh_differences %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(domain=factor(domain, levels=domains)) %>% 
    dplyr::arrange(domain) #%>% 
    # dplyr::mutate(x2019=ifelse(is.na(x2019), 0,x2019),
    #               x2025=ifelse(is.na(x2025), 0,x2025),
    #               difference=ifelse((is.na(difference) & is.na(x2019)),x2025, difference),
    #               difference=ifelse((is.na(difference) & !is.na(x2019)),-x2019, difference))
    # 

  cat('<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 20px;">\n')

# Loop through boxes
  for(i in 1:nrow(imd_bh_differences)){
    box_class <- ifelse(i == 1, "text-box text-box-first", "text-box")
    
    cat('<div class="', box_class, '">', sep = "")
    cat('<span class="number">', paste0(round(imd_bh_differences$x2025[i],1),"%"), '</span><br>', sep = "")
    cat('<span class="description">',paste0("of our population live a ", imd_bh_differences$domain[i], " Core 20   area."), '</span>', sep = "")
  cat('<span class="description">',paste0(" This is an ",round(imd_bh_differences$difference[i],1), "% point change since 2019" ),   '</span>', sep = "")
    cat('</div>\n')
  }
  
  cat('</div>\n\n')  # close flex container and add spacing
}
```
